# Tool reference

<!-- GENERATED by `TiaMcpServer.exe --dump-tools markdown`. Do not edit by hand. -->

102 tools: 46 read-only, 26 write, 16 write that can turn destructive, 14 always destructive.

| Safety class | Meaning | Available with |
|---|---|---|
| read-only | Never changes the project. May write an export file where you tell it to. | `--access readonly`, `write`, `full` |
| write | Creates objects or changes properties. Nothing existing is removed. | `--access write`, `full` |
| **destructive** | Deletes or replaces existing content, or discards unsaved work. Refused without `confirm: true`. | `--access full` |

See [SAFETY.md](SAFETY.md) for the full safety model.

## Details

### tia_connect

*Connect to TIA Portal* - group `core` - read-only

Connect this server to TIA Portal. Call this first. 'attach' (default) joins the TIA Portal the user already has open; 'new_ui' / 'new_headless' start a fresh instance with / without a window. Changes nothing in the project. The first connection after the server is (re)built makes TIA Portal show an Openness access prompt that the user must accept.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string |  | attach \| new_ui \| new_headless (default attach) |
| `projectPath` | string |  | attach only: prefer the running instance that has this .apNN project open |

### tia_state

*Connection state* - group `core` - read-only

Connection state, the open project, whether it has unsaved changes, and how this server is configured (access level, tool groups, backups).

### tia_doctor

*Check the environment* - group `core` - read-only

Checks the prerequisites for talking to TIA Portal: Openness installed, the Windows user in the 'Siemens TIA Openness' group, running TIA instances, connection and project. Works before tia_connect; use it when connecting fails.

### tia_open_project

*Open a project* - group `core` - read-only

Open a TIA Portal project file in the connected instance. Does not modify the project. TIA holds one project at a time: prefer tia_connect (attach) when the user already has it open.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Absolute path to the project file (.ap20) |

### tia_save_project

*Save the project* - group `core` - write

Save the open project to disk. This is the point of no return: until it is called, every change made through this server lives only in TIA Portal's memory and can be undone or discarded by closing without saving. Only save when the user asks for it. Refused when the server runs with --no-save.

### tia_close_project

*Close the project* - group `core` - **destructive**

Close the open project. Unsaved changes are LOST unless save:true. Closes it in the user's TIA Portal window too when attached.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `save` | boolean |  | Save before closing (default false: unsaved changes are discarded) |
| `confirm` | boolean | yes | Must be true. Set true only after the user has approved this specific deletion/overwrite (an explicit instruction to build or iterate on these objects counts). Without it the call is refused. |

### tia_project_info

*Project information* - group `core` - read-only

Project metadata: path, author, TIA version, last modification, unsaved-changes flag, project languages (needed for multilingual texts), installed products it uses, and device names.

### tia_archive_project

*Archive the project (backup)* - group `core` - read-only

Write a compressed archive (.zapNN) of the project to disk as a restore point. Does not modify the project. Take it BEFORE large or destructive changes: TIA refuses to archive a project that has unsaved changes. Restore in TIA Portal with Project > Retrieve.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `targetDir` | string |  | Directory for the archive; must be outside the project folder (default: the server's backup folder) |
| `name` | string |  | Archive file name without extension (default: <project>_<timestamp>) |
| `compressed` | boolean |  | Compress the archive (default true) |

### tia_list_devices

*List devices* - group `core` - read-only

All devices in the project and the software each one holds: 'plc', 'hmiUnified' (WinCC Unified) or 'hmiClassic' (Comfort/Basic). The software name is what the 'device' argument of the other tools expects.

### tia_compile

*Compile* - group `core` - write

Compile a PLC, an HMI or a single block and return the compiler messages. Changes the compile state of the project, not its logic. Always read the messages: a successful import does not mean the code is correct. Nothing is downloaded to the PLC.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC or HMI name (default: first PLC) |
| `block` | string |  | Compile only this block or PLC data type |
| `scope` | string |  | For a PLC: software (default) \| hardware \| all |

### tia_list_blocks

*List blocks* - group `plc` - read-only

List the program blocks (OB/FB/FC/DB) of a PLC with number, language, folder, consistency and know-how protection.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |

### tia_read_block

*Read a block* - group `plc` - read-only

Return the content of a block or PLC data type inline: source text for SCL/STL blocks, DBs and UDTs; SimaticML XML for graphical blocks (LAD/FBD/GRAPH). The usual way to read existing code before changing it. Fails while TIA is online.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |
| `block` | string | yes | Block or PLC data type name |
| `format` | string |  | auto (default) \| source \| xml |
| `maxChars` | integer |  | Cut the content at this many characters (default 60000, 0 = no limit) |

### tia_get_block_interface

*Block interface* - group `plc` - read-only

The interface of a block (Input/Output/InOut/Static/Temp/Constant members with data types, start values and comments), or the members of a DB or PLC data type. Use it to call a block or address a DB correctly. The object must be consistent (compiled).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |
| `block` | string | yes | Block or PLC data type name |

### tia_export_block

*Export block (XML file)* - group `plc` - read-only

Export a block or PLC data type to a SimaticML XML file on disk. Does not modify the project; overwrites <outDir>/<name>.xml. Only consistent (compiled) objects can be exported.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |
| `block` | string | yes | Block or PLC data type name |
| `outDir` | string | yes | Output directory for the XML file |

### tia_export_source

*Export source (text file)* - group `plc` - read-only

Generate the source text of a block or PLC data type to a file (.scl, .db, .udt or .awl). Does not modify the project; overwrites the file. Not available for graphical blocks or while online.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |
| `block` | string | yes | Block or PLC data type name |
| `outDir` | string | yes | Output directory for the source file |
| `withDependencies` | boolean |  | Also include the blocks and types this one depends on (default false) |

### tia_get_cross_references

*Cross-references* - group `plc` - read-only

Where a block, PLC data type, PLC tag or tag table is used, and what it uses. Check this before deleting or renaming anything.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |
| `name` | string | yes | Name of the block, data type, tag or tag table |
| `filter` | string |  | AllObjects (default) \| ObjectsWithReferences \| ObjectsWithoutReferences \| UnusedObjects |
| `maxLocations` | integer |  | Stop after this many use locations (default 200) |

### tia_import_scl

*Write blocks from SCL source* - group `plc` - write / **destructive** when the source redefines blocks or data types that already exist

Generate blocks (FB/FC/OB/DB) or PLC data types from SCL-family source, given inline or as a file. THE way to write PLC logic. New objects are simply created. If the source redefines an object that already exists, TIA replaces it in place: that needs confirm:true, and the old version is backed up first (path returned). The generated objects are compiled and the compiler messages returned: TIA accepts source with errors silently, so read errorCount. Fails while TIA is online.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |
| `source` | string |  | Source text inline (use this or sclPath) |
| `sclPath` | string |  | Absolute path to a .scl / .db / .udt source file (use this or source) |
| `name` | string |  | Name for the inline source (only labels it in TIA) |
| `group` | string |  | Block folder to generate into, e.g. "Machine/Station1" (created if missing; default: root) |
| `keepSource` | boolean |  | Keep the external source object in the project (default false) |
| `compile` | boolean |  | Compile the generated objects and return the messages (default true) |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Required when the source redefines blocks or data types that already exist. Set true only after the user has approved this specific deletion/overwrite (an explicit instruction to build or iterate on these objects counts). Without it the call is refused. |

### tia_import_block

*Import block (SimaticML XML)* - group `plc` - write / **destructive** when overwrite:true

Import a block from SimaticML XML, inline or from a file. Use for LAD/FBD/GRAPH blocks or to restore an export. Without overwrite an existing block makes it fail; with overwrite:true the existing block is replaced (backed up first).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |
| `xml` | string |  | SimaticML document inline (use this or xmlPath) |
| `xmlPath` | string |  | Absolute path to the SimaticML XML file (use this or xml) |
| `group` | string |  | Block folder to import into (default: the existing block's folder, else root) |
| `overwrite` | boolean |  | Replace the block if it already exists (default false) |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Required when overwrite:true. Set true only after the user has approved this specific deletion/overwrite (an explicit instruction to build or iterate on these objects counts). Without it the call is refused. |

### tia_create_lad_block

*Create a LAD block* - group `plc` - write / **destructive** when overwrite:true

Create a ladder (LAD) FB, FC or OB from a structured description of its rungs; the XML, UIds and wires are generated for you, then the block is imported and compiled. Each network is series logic in 'elements' ending in 'outputs'. A seal-in is one network: elements=[branch[[contact Start],[contact Motor]], contact Stop negated], outputs=[coil Motor]. Operands: a PLC tag (Tag), a DB member ("DB".Member), a local (#name) or a constant (T#5s, 10). Use dryRun:true to validate and see the XML without touching TIA. A clean compile does not prove the logic: ask the user to review it.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |
| `name` | string | yes | Block name |
| `type` | string |  | FB (default) \| FC \| OB |
| `number` | integer |  | Block number (default: assigned automatically) |
| `interface` | object |  | Interface members by section. FB: input/output/inOut/static/temp/constant; FC: no static; OB: input/temp/constant. |
| `networks` | array | yes | Networks (rungs), in order. |
| `culture` | string |  | Project language for network titles/comments, e.g. en-US (see tia_project_info). Omit to leave them out. |
| `group` | string |  | Block folder to create the block in (default: root) |
| `overwrite` | boolean |  | Replace an existing block of the same name (default false) |
| `compile` | boolean |  | Compile after importing (default true) |
| `dryRun` | boolean |  | Only validate and return the generated XML; TIA is not touched |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Required when overwrite:true. Set true only after the user has approved this specific deletion/overwrite (an explicit instruction to build or iterate on these objects counts). Without it the call is refused. |

### tia_create_block_group

*Create a block folder* - group `plc` - write

Create a folder (group) under Program blocks. Nested paths are created as needed; an existing folder is left as it is.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |
| `path` | string | yes | Folder path, e.g. "Machine/Station1" |

### tia_delete_block_group

*Delete an empty block folder* - group `plc` - **destructive**

Delete a folder under Program blocks. Only an EMPTY folder is deleted: if it still holds blocks or subfolders the call fails and nothing is removed.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |
| `path` | string | yes | Folder path, e.g. "Machine/Station1" |
| `confirm` | boolean | yes | Must be true. Set true only after the user has approved this specific deletion/overwrite (an explicit instruction to build or iterate on these objects counts). Without it the call is refused. |

### tia_delete_block

*Delete a block* - group `plc` - **destructive**

Delete a program block. Its source (or XML) is backed up first and the path returned, but calls to it elsewhere in the program break. Check tia_get_cross_references first.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (optional: defaults to the first PLC) |
| `block` | string | yes | Name of the block to delete |

### tia_hmi_set_widget_property

*Set an item property* - group `hmi` - write

Set one property of a screen item (or of the screen) by name; the value is converted to the property's type (number, bool, enum name, colour, text). Nested parts use a dotted path: "Font.Size", "Content.ContentMode". Collection elements use brackets: "TrendAreas[0]" takes an existing element by position (index = current count appends a new one, e.g. "Trends[1]" when there is one trend), "TrendAreas[area1].LeftValueAxes[ax].BeginValue" takes it by name and creates it if missing. Multilingual texts take one language with '@culture': "Text@en-US", "TrendAreas[0].Trends[1].DisplayName@en-US" (without it every language gets the same text). The property is read back afterwards: 'set' is true only if it now holds the requested value (TIA sometimes ignores an assignment without an error), 'value' is what it reads and 'previous' what it was. Discover properties with tia_hmi_get_item.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | HMI name (optional: defaults to the first WinCC Unified HMI) |
| `screen` | string | yes | Screen name |
| `item` | string | yes | Screen item name, or "@screen" for the screen itself |
| `property` | string | yes | Property name or dotted path, e.g. BackColor, Font.Size, IOFieldType, Visible, TrendAreas[a1].Trends[t1].LineColor |
| `value` | string | yes | New value as text |

### tia_hmi_get_software_object

*Read an HMI software object* - group `hmi` - read-only

Read any object of the WinCC Unified HMI software (not a screen item) by path from the HMI software: "AlarmClasses" lists the alarm classes, "AlarmClasses[Alarm].RaisedState" shows one state's colours, "RuntimeSettings" the runtime settings. Collections list their elements; objects list their simple properties and the names of their parts. Empty path = the software root.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | HMI name (optional: defaults to the first WinCC Unified HMI) |
| `path` | string |  | Path from the HMI software, e.g. AlarmClasses[Alarm].RaisedState (empty = root) |

Make a colour property (e.g. BackColor) follow a Bool HMI tag: one colour when false, another when true. Native tag dynamization with a two-entry mapping table - the reliable way to show a feedback state.

| `confirm` | boolean |  | Required when dryRun:false. Set true only after the user has approved this specific deletion/overwrite (an explicit instruction to build or iterate on these objects counts). Without it the call is refused. |

### tia_dump_plc_protection

*PLC protection settings* - group `hardware` - read-only

The PLC's protection access level and the access/connection-related attributes (PUT/GET, secure communication), to diagnose why an HMI or S7 client cannot connect. Passwords are not read.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (default: first PLC) |

### tia_s7_read

*Live read: raw bytes* - group `s7` - read-only

Read raw bytes from a memory area of the running PLC; returns hex, a byte array and printable ASCII. For typed values prefer tia_s7_read_values / tia_s7_read_tags. Optimized DBs cannot be read by offset: use a non-optimized DB, or I/Q/M. Talks to the running PLC over the network, independently of TIA Portal; needs 'Permit access with PUT/GET communication' enabled on the CPU. Never writes to the PLC.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip` | string |  | PLC IP address (default: last one used, else the address configured in the project) |
| `area` | string | yes | DB \| I \| Q \| M |
| `db` | integer |  | DB number (area DB only) |
| `start` | integer | yes | Start byte offset, e.g. 68 for %IB68 |
| `size` | integer | yes | Number of bytes (1-8192) |
| `rack` | integer |  | Rack (default 0) |
| `slot` | integer |  | Slot (default 1 for S7-1200/1500) |

### tia_s7_read_values

*Live read: typed values by address* - group `s7` - read-only

Read typed values from the running PLC by absolute address (I0.0, QB4, MW10, MD20, DB5.DBX0.1, DB5.DBW2, DB5.DBD4). Several in one call; one failing address does not stop the others. Talks to the running PLC over the network, independently of TIA Portal; needs 'Permit access with PUT/GET communication' enabled on the CPU. Never writes to the PLC.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip` | string |  | PLC IP address (default: last one used, else the address configured in the project) |
| `items` | array | yes | Values to read |
| `rack` | integer |  | Rack (default 0) |
| `slot` | integer |  | Slot (default 1 for S7-1200/1500) |

### tia_s7_read_tags

*Live read: PLC tags by name* - group `s7` - read-only

Read the live value of PLC tags by NAME: address and data type are taken from the project's tag tables (so TIA must be connected), the value from the running PLC. Only tags with an absolute address (I/Q/M); DB members are read by address with tia_s7_read_values. Talks to the running PLC over the network, independently of TIA Portal; needs 'Permit access with PUT/GET communication' enabled on the CPU. Never writes to the PLC.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | PLC name (default: first PLC) |
| `tags` | array | yes | PLC tag names |
| `ip` | string |  | PLC IP address (default: last one used, else the address configured in the project) |
| `rack` | integer |  | Rack (default 0) |
| `slot` | integer |  | Slot (default 1 for S7-1200/1500) |

### tia_s7_cpu_info

*Live read: CPU status* - group `s7` - read-only

RUN/STOP state and article number of the running CPU (plus module and station name where the CPU answers that query; S7-1200/1500 often do not). Talks to the running PLC over the network, independently of TIA Portal; needs 'Permit access with PUT/GET communication' enabled on the CPU. Never writes to the PLC.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip` | string |  | PLC IP address (default: last one used, else the address configured in the project) |
| `rack` | integer |  | Rack (default 0) |
| `slot` | integer |  | Slot (default 1 for S7-1200/1500) |
